items.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Norris has performed with the Savoy Sultans, George Wein’s All Stars, and in numerous Broadway shows.

ctx.x: Saxophonist Norris Turney was born in Wilmington, Ohio on September 8, 1921. He first found work with territory bands led by Jeter Pillars and Tiny Bradshaw, later moving to New York to work with Billy Eckstine. Norris also excelled on flute and clarinet and was tapped to sub for Johnny Hodges in 1969.

He took over the lead alto chair in the Ellington Orchestra after Johnny passed away, and led the reed section until 1973. Norris has performed with the Savoy Sultans, George Wein’s All Stars, and in numerous Broadway shows. His playing manages to bridge the world of swing and bebop, and he is a familiar presence at jazz festivals and parties across the country. His latest recording is “Big, Sweet and Blue.”
Norris was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 11, 1997, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
